findings: All ten example/script files read whole. Original Python alpharemover executed on three independently specified RGBA pixels: transparent black becomes white, half-alpha black becomes 127 gray, opaque RGB unchanged.

Dart preprocessing explicitly copies raw RGB and discards alpha; Python composites RGBA against white. This gives different hash inputs for transparency; no original Dart runtime claim. Python non-RGBA modes bypass this helper.

Z preprocessing differs: Python uses LANCZOS then NumPy percentile/interpolation over 0..99; Dart default copyResize, rounded 0..99 rank samples, first matching interval mapped to i/99*255 without interpolation. Same z suffix does not establish same recipe.

Icon grouping excludes ERROR and all-zero hash, groups exact hash strings without file/pixel verification, filters unknown repository URL patterns, and can retain singleton visible groups after filtering.

Sources and generated URLs use floating main/master branches; requirements contain unpinned Pillow/NumPy/imagehash. Scripts swallow per-image/hash failures and print input-count processed even when errors occur. Setup/conversion/clone scripts inspected, not executed.
